page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with Hebrew lemmata at the left of each entry, Latin glosses and Biblical references in the body. No marginal notes. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. Catchword "& tùm" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: Et ex dividentibus ungulam, Lev.11.4. cum defectu ' in medio, juxta Masorethas. Fœm. מַפְרִסֶת[?] Dividens, Lev.11.3. dicitur, tantùm in hac Conjugatione de Ungula animalium divisa vel scissa.
פֶּרֶס[?] m. Olsifraga, aquilæ species immunda, Levit.11.13. Alii aliter.

פַּרְסָה f. Ungula, à Fissura, Levit.11.3. Plural. פָּרְסוֹת Ungulæ, Lev.11.3. Constr. פָּרְסוֹת Jef.5.28. Aff. וּפַרְסָתְךָ Et ungulas tuas, Mich.4.13. Et masc. וּפַרְסֵיהֶן Et ungulas earum, Zach.11.16.

פָּרַע Nudavit, Retexit: Abstraxit, Abjecit, Rejecit, Destituit: Abstraxit se, Recessit, Averit se, Retrocessit: Item Ulus est, ex usu Chaldaico: Præter. פָּרַע Et reteget, Num.5.18. כִּי פָּרְעָה Quòd nudas-fet eum, Exod.22.25. Partic. præsens, פּוֹרֵעַ Abstrahens, Rejiciens, Prov.13.18. Partic. passivum, פָּרוּעַ Retectum, Lev.13.45. Infin. בְּפָרֵעַ In ulciscendo, Jud.5.2. Imperat. פָּרְעֵהוּ Abstrahe, Abjice eam, Prov.4.15. Fut. אֶפְרַע Abstra-hám me, Retrocedam, Ezech.24.14. יִפְרַע Reteget, Lev.21. v.10. תִּפְרְעוּ Abstrahite vos, Prov.8.33. וַתִּפְרְעוּ Et rejecisti, Prov.1.25. Niph. Futur. יִפָּרַע Abstrahitur, Averti se, Prov.29.18. Hiph. Præt. הִפְרִיעַ Abstractionem vel Aversionem fecerat, scil. Rex Achas, 2.Par.28.19. Fut. תַּפְרִיעוּ Abstrahitis, Exod.5.4.
פֶּרַע m. Coma, Num.6.5. quia quò ma-gis nutritur, eò magis Retegitur.
פָּרְעָה f. Ultio: Plural. פִּרְעוֹת Ultiones, Judic.5. v.2. Constr. פִּרְעוֹת Deut.32.42.
* פָּרְעשׁ m. Pulex: אַחֲרֵי פַּרְעשׁ אֶחָד Post pulicem unum, 1.Sam.24.15.
פָּרַץ Rupit, Erupit, Difrupit, Irrupit, Perrupit, Ruptura fecit, Effregit: Item, Urfit, Insitit,

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and several Hebrew forms are uncertain at this scan resolution; marked [?] where doubtful. "Insitit" is read with some doubt. The word "fecerat" in the Hiphil gloss is partly obscured. The Latin "nudas-fet" and "ma-gis" hyphenations are as printed at the line ends. The catchword "& tùm" is in the printed position below the last line and is kept out of the text. Italic and roman type in the Latin glosses is approximated from the scan.
